title: Privatisation projects: three projects, seven objectives

source.citation: Brauers, W. K. M., Zavadskas, E. K. (2006). The MOORA method and its application to privatization in a transition economy. Control and Cybernetics, 35(2), 445-469.
source.note: The journal issued no DOI; the European Digital Mathematics Library record is the stable identifier. Read from the open-access copy in the Polish Library of Science.

deviations.note: The printed maximal deviation of B is its investment deviation 0.2517544 truncated to five decimals (0.25174); rounded it is 0.25175.

notes: Objectives: internal rate of return (%), payback period (years, minimised), productivity increase (%), new investment, new employment (jobs), discounted value added, balance of payments. All but payback are maximised.

No weights: the original MOORA treats all objectives as equally important (Section 4 discusses importance coefficients and sub-objectives as options). The ratio system adds the normalised maximised objectives and subtracts the minimised ones; a weighted variant multiplies each ratio by w_j before summing.

Vector normalisation x_ij / sqrt(sum_i x_ij^2) (Eq. 2). The reference point is the best normalised value per objective, and alternatives are ranked by the smallest maximal (Tchebycheff) deviation from it (Eq. 4).
The paper prints values to between three and nine decimals; each table uses the smallest number of decimals it prints in that block.
